page: OVHcloud b2-15 is a general-purpose virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Haswell processor with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 15.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 100 GB local SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the b2-15 delivers modest compute performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 959.69 falls into the bottom 10%, while the multi-core score of 3669.99 is in the bottom 25%. Similarly, the PassMark CPU score of 5541.45 is categorized as weak. However, memory performance is more balanced, with a cached read-only small block memory bandwidth of 347.69 GB/sec and a PassMark memory score of 1982.04, both placing in the middle 50%. Large block uncached read and write memory bandwidths are lower, registering at 37.17 GB/sec and 22.32 GB/sec respectively.

In terms of workload execution, the server performs adequately for database operations and basic caching, with PassMark database operations scoring 2698.32 and Redis SET operations reaching 5.93 million operations per second. It is less suited for intensive tasks; static web serving throughput is limited to 4.56 GB/sec, and LLM inference on a medium 7B model is poor, yielding 10.43 tokens per second for prompt processing. Given the dedicated CPU allocation combined with older Intel Haswell architecture, this server offers a stable, non-burstable resource profile for general-purpose workloads, development environments, and lightweight database applications where high-end compute performance is not a primary requirement.
